Those worries intensified after Democrats won sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections, which could bring moratoriums or tighter restrictions on data center construction in some states. The perceived risk of a construction slowdown pushed AI-related stocks sharply lower on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite closing down 5.5%, its worst day since April 2025 and in correction territory. Hank Calenti, global markets strategist at SMBC, said banks may sell more debt depending on whether the discount they accept outweighs the benefit of freeing cash for new lending. Pruksa Iamthongthong, head of APAC equities at Aberdeen Investments, said near-term volatility could continue as markets assess possible delays to U.S. data center construction and limits on compute capacity.

Earlier this year, Wall Street lenders including JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley were reported to be exploring ways to reduce their exposure to data center construction lending. According to a Financial Times report from May 3, those approaches include selling portions of debt to non-bank lenders and using significant risk transfers that shift part of a bank's credit risk to investors. These steps are intended to free up balance sheet capacity for banks. The ING auction is one of the latest examples of that effort.

Articles.Title: AI debt concerns grow as ING reportedly seeks buyers for $500 million of data center loans

stories.Headline: Synology sets out Singapore’s next step in turning AI ambition into business results
stories.Summary:
Synology, a network-attached storage and data backup company founded in Taiwan in 2000, used its Annual Press Event 2026 in Singapore on November 6, 2026 to lay out how businesses there can turn AI ambitions into lasting results. The company said AI helps people do their work better and lets firms respond more effectively to customers, but those gains depend on data that teams can trust and systems that can recover from disruption. Synology's Southeast Asia Head, Antoine Yang, framed the company's aim as helping organizations sustain those gains as adoption grows. The survey Synology cited found that 71.3% of Singapore respondents rank data security and privacy as their top concern, ahead of data quality and availability at 46.3% and high implementation costs at 41.7%. It also found that 58.7% prioritize hybrid or on-premises infrastructure, compared with just 9.7% who prioritize public cloud.

Although 76% of respondents said they are confident they could recover quickly from ransomware while keeping backups protected, only 26.9% said they were very confident. Nearly 30% reported having no visibility into how data submitted to third-party AI tools is handled. Synology's Singapore Country Manager, Emily Oh, said businesses expanding their data infrastructure also need assurance that essential services can recover when disruption occurs. The company built its priorities around scalable data infrastructure, stronger cyber resilience, and productive AI adoption with greater control over business data. Its 2026 launches include the PAS7700, its first NVMe SSD storage solution for mission-critical workloads, along with new FS and RS series storage and the DSM 7.4 operating system.

On the resilience side, it highlighted the ActiveProtect appliances, the ActiveProtect Manager 2.0 software, and the DP5200, a 1U appliance sold without recurring subscription fees. Synology also described AI tools for the workplace, including Synology Office Suite, which offers on-premises AI assistance for documents, presentations and spreadsheet formulas, plus ChatPlus and Meet for messaging and online meetings. Its DVA7400 surveillance appliance applies AI to detection and search to help teams investigate incidents. The company previewed upcoming scale-out storage and hybrid surveillance solutions meant to help enterprises grow as data volumes increase. Oh said that when businesses trust how their data is managed and protected, they are better positioned to turn AI initiatives into lasting business results.

Articles.Title: Synology sets out Singapore’s next step in turning AI ambition into business results - The Business Times

stories.Headline: AI could boost Italy-China innovation cooperation: report - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Italy and China could use artificial intelligence to link their different industrial strengths, according to a report presented by the Italy-China Foundation in Rome on Thursday, November 5, 2026. The report argues that China's technological rise should not be viewed only as competition and points instead to chances for collaboration in innovation and AI. It says China offers scale, manufacturing capacity and speed in turning technologies into production, while Italy is strong in industrial expertise, specialized production and design. Together, the report suggests, these strengths could support advanced manufacturing and new supply chains for high-value products.

The report also notes that China's innovation ecosystem keeps growing, with more than 6,600 AI companies operating in the country as of June 2026. Mario Boselli, president of the foundation, said companies now face greater geopolitical and technological uncertainty, which makes analytical tools and knowledge more important for strategic decisions. A separate story from China Daily, dated November 4, 2026, covers a different AI relationship, between the United States and China. Its focus is safety rather than commerce, and it describes shared risks that could push the two countries toward cooperation despite their rivalry. Those risks include misuse of AI for biological weapons and cyberattacks.

Steve Westly, founder and managing partner of The Westly Group, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm, says these dangers could force a US-China agreement and that the sooner it happens the better. The two governments announced in September a bilateral dialogue on AI risks and benefits and agreed to set up a communication channel for AI incidents. China said the next dialogue would take place in November, and the White House said the next exchange would occur by that month. Liang Min, managing director of Stanford University's Bits & Watts Initiative, argues that cooperation on safety can coexist with competition, pointing to joint work on nuclear power plant safety as a precedent.

The article describes the risks in concrete terms, citing the International AI Safety Report 2026, which documents systems that can find software vulnerabilities and assist with tasks relevant to biological misuse. In one cybersecurity competition, an AI agent identified 77 percent of vulnerabilities in real software and placed in the top 5 percent of more than 400 mostly human teams. A Brookings Institution commentary from July proposes regular technical exchanges on methods for assessing and reducing risks such as cyber threats and weapons-related misuse. Westly says political mistrust remains the main barrier, and that the political and technological challenges will be harder to resolve than energy constraints.

Articles.Title: AI could boost Italy-China innovation cooperation: report - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Kenya, China explore cooperation on AI infrastructure and digital skills
stories.Summary:
Kenya and China are exploring cooperation in artificial intelligence, cloud computing and digital skills development, according to a report published on November 5, 2026. A proposed grant of $180 million is expected to support the first phase of an AI cloud data project in Eldoret, in western Kenya. Officials say the project would strengthen the country's AI and cloud computing infrastructure. A separate proposed capacity-building program would train Kenyan youth, professionals and institutions to develop, manage and deploy AI technologies. The proposals were discussed at a meeting that William Kabogo, the cabinet secretary for information, communications and the digital economy, held with Chinese Ambassador to Kenya Guo Haiyan.

Kabogo said in a statement after the Wednesday meeting that the talks aimed to support Kenya's digital transformation. He said any partnerships and investments must respect national priorities, data sovereignty requirements and existing ICT regulations. The discussions also covered plans to speed up the digitization of government services so they are more accessible, efficient and responsive to citizens. Kabogo added that Kenya wants to explore access to up to $5 billion set aside through the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization for international cooperation in the sector. The report does not say whether any of these proposals has been finalized.

The talks come as Kenya works to build its domestic AI capabilities and position itself as a regional technology hub. In March 2025, the country launched its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2030, which sets out plans to expand AI infrastructure, strengthen data governance and promote local research, innovation and commercialization. The strategy also names skills development as a priority for preparing the workforce for an economy that is becoming increasingly driven by AI. The articles tie the Eldoret project and the training program to these existing national goals. They do not give a timeline for when the grant might be confirmed or when the first phase would begin.

Articles.Title: Kenya, China explore cooperation on AI infrastructure and digital skills - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: Cisco exec sees China holding sway in industrial AI
stories.Summary:
China's large manufacturing base could give it an advantage in industrial artificial intelligence, according to David Siroky, Cisco's AI architecture lead for Asia Pacific, Japan and Greater China. He told China Daily on Wednesday, on the sidelines of the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Zhejiang province, that factories supply the operational data needed to train models that detect defects and predict equipment failures. Siroky said China has spent more than two decades building the production lines and sensors that generate that data. The summit concluded on Thursday. Siroky pointed to automotive assembly as an example of the economics involved.

A paint flaw fixed on a domestic line costs far less than one found after a vehicle has been shipped to an export market such as Australia. BMW Group said its plant in Shenyang, Liaoning province, uses an AI-assisted computer vision system in its paint shop to scan every car for micro-scratches and surface imperfections. The system marks affected areas with precision lasers so they can be repaired quickly. Such deployments are being used across several industries. China accounted for 59 percent of the industrial robots installed worldwide in 2025, with 354,000 new installations, according to the International Federation of Robotics.

That level of automation supports the spread of these capabilities. Turning factory data into training material requires further work, and guidelines published in January by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and seven other government bodies describe how manufacturers should collect, clean and label it. The guidelines set a target of building 100 high-quality industrial datasets by 2027 for uses including process control and fault diagnosis. For Cisco, the fastest-growing demand in China is for high-speed networking that links the many graphics processing units needed to train or fine-tune large models across server racks, Siroky said. Companies often learn how much network capacity they need only after moving a project beyond a pilot, and some find their networks lack throughput or their facilities cannot supply enough power for dense GPU clusters.

Cisco's overall product revenue in China rose 23 percent year on year in the fiscal year ended July 25, according to its annual report. Siroky added that despite rapid progress over the past two years, the broader transformation has only begun. At the software level, enterprises are increasingly turning to open-source models from domestic developers such as DeepSeek and Alibaba's Qwen, mainly to control costs. Siroky said smaller, targeted models deployed on on-premise infrastructure avoid recurring per-query cloud fees after the initial hardware investment. On-premise deployment also helps organizations such as hospitals that must analyze sensitive records without sending data beyond their internal networks.

Articles.Title: Cisco exec sees China holding sway in industrial AI - China Daily

stories.Headline: Shenzhen's AI robotics company Astribot to scale up business
stories.Summary:
Astribot, an AI robotics company based in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, said it will expand its product deliveries in 2027 by launching robotic products for individual users. The company plans to move gradually into home settings as well. The announcement came from Fang Ke, co-founder and chief financial officer of Astribot, who spoke at the China-Global Innovation Forum held in Hong Kong on a Monday as part of Hong Kong Fintech Week. The article does not specify the exact date of the forum beyond that it was a Monday, and it was published on November 5, 2026.

Fang said the company is now moving from technology demonstration and small-scale production to replicable orders, and next will focus on scaling up its business. Its priorities include cost control, product delivery and technology iteration. Astribot began mass production in 2025, and developers and commercial service clients have made repeat purchases, with some clients expanding their delivery scale in specific scenarios. The company's S and T robotic series has a total production capacity of 10,000 units.

Astribot's products are deployed across retail, cultural tourism, industry, research and education. Its independently developed Robot MART has been in use in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou since November 2025. Fang also said the company has partnered with enterprises to apply its products in industrial settings. As deliveries and commercial applications grow, Astribot has increased spending on research and development, talent recruitment and capacity building.

The company announced in October a new financing round worth 1 billion yuan, or about $150 million, its fourth round since March. According to the article, the funds will support continued technological innovation and commercialization. Fang framed the company's direction as bringing embodied intelligence from specialized applications into everyday life, while improving the operational and human-machine interaction capabilities of its robots. The article does not give further details on the timing or scale of the planned home products.

Articles.Title: Shenzhen's AI robotics company Astribot to scale up business - China Daily

stories.Headline: Lost in translation? AI helps Chinese micro-dramas go global
stories.Summary:
Chinese micro-dramas, short serialized shows built around cliffhangers, are reaching audiences abroad, and a Wuhan artificial intelligence company is helping them cross language barriers. Transn IOL Technology, based in Wuhan, Hubei province, has translated and dubbed more than 20,000 such productions for markets including North America, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East. The reporting, published by China Daily on November 6, 2026, describes how the translation challenge goes beyond words. Terms like "bengong," an imperial woman's way of referring to herself, are often rendered simply as "I" so that viewers are not confused.

The company has built a workflow that combines automated translation, human review, and voice cloning on its TaiHow Video platform. The system separates dialogue from background sound, translates scripts in context, generates multilingual dubbing, and reassembles the audio. Transn's proprietary large language model handles the bulk of the work, and several AI agents cross-check one another before language experts carry out two rounds of human review. According to the company's vice-president Shi Xin, an hour of video can be processed at the automated stage in roughly the same time it takes to watch it, with a market-test version ready in one or two days and a polished version in three to five. A fully manual process takes at least two weeks, and Transn says AI has cut its overall translation and dubbing costs by around 30 percent.

Transn's vice-president Fu Qiang described the approach as machines checking machines before people step in, and the company's leaders say human translators still handle what machines cannot. Cultural concepts such as the "live-in son-in-law" carry family expectations with no direct equivalent, and imperial ranks require consistent terminology across a series. Reviewers correct misunderstandings and make sure characters' personalities and emotions survive translation. Shi also said tastes vary by market, with North American viewers favoring romance and fantasy, family-centered stories resonating in Southeast Asia, and Middle Eastern audiences drawn to romance and inheritance plots.

The market behind this work is growing quickly. DataEye Research Institute expects the micro-drama market outside China to exceed $6 billion this year, and Sensor Tower reported that global downloads of short-drama apps passed 850 million in the first quarter of 2026, up 140 percent year on year. Transn's revenue from its film and cultural translation business rose 29.8 percent year on year in the first half of 2026, although its gross profit margin fell by 13.19 percentage points, according to its interim report. The company's next challenge, as the article frames it, is making translated stories feel natural to local audiences while keeping pace in a fast-moving entertainment market.

Articles.Title: Lost in translation? AI helps Chinese micro-dramas go global - China Daily

stories.Headline: Cyrus Hodes: Open-source AI development should balance openness and safety
stories.Summary:
The articles report remarks by Cyrus Hodes at the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, held in Wuzhen, in East China's Zhejiang province. Hodes, who is a member of the OECD Expert Group on AI Future and founder of AI Safety Connect, spoke about open-source artificial intelligence. The reports say he described it as a tool with the potential to spread knowledge around the world. He also said it could help countries that do not yet have the capacity to build and deploy such technologies themselves. The piece was published on November 5, 2026.

Hodes argued that AI models should be developed and released with safety as a core consideration. The articles do not spell out any specific rule, deadline or figure attached to that position. Instead, they describe his call as a general emphasis on responsible design before release. The coverage presents this as part of a broader message that openness and safety should be weighed together.

Hodes also referred to a report that was released at the Wuzhen Summit. According to the articles, he used that report to stress the importance of setting up coordinated mechanisms among the countries that are leading discussions on AI development. The articles do not name the report's authors or list its specific recommendations. They also do not describe any agreed mechanism, participating countries or timetable for creating one.

The articles offer no further context about how these coordinated mechanisms would work or what steps might follow the summit. They are short and include an unrelated item about an exhibition in Yunnan province. Beyond Hodes's remarks and the report he cited, nothing more is available in the material provided. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Cyrus Hodes: Open-source AI development should balance openness and safety - China Daily

stories.Headline: AI offers answers, curiosity drives discovery
stories.Summary:
Nobel Prize-winning chemist Michael Levitt, who shared the 2013 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, spoke at the 2026 World Laureates Forum in Shanghai about the role of curiosity and artificial intelligence in scientific work. He urged young researchers around the world to take up both. Levitt, a professor of structural biology at Stanford University, said that asking good questions matters most when working with AI. He described AI as something like a conversation partner that offers many answers, which is why a researcher needs curiosity to choose among them.

Levitt said that scientists must be open-minded yet skeptical, since AI does not always give correct information. In his own practice, he said, he checks an AI answer by asking someone else, and he tends to trust a result only when two sources agree. He praised the rapid spread of AI in China, across education and research, and called China's use of the technology very strong. He also said he was pleased to see AI so widely adopted there. Levitt added that a Nobel Prize brings a wider responsibility, which he compared to acting as a diplomat of science.

Levitt said he wants as many young people as possible to enter science, because he believes the field benefits the world and can produce discoveries with large effects. He pointed to the forum as a rare setting where established laureates and emerging researchers exchange ideas. He recalled hearing five lectures on very different subjects that he said would be almost impossible to hear anywhere else. He stressed that young people are the focus of the forum and that new ideas usually come from them. He said the future belongs to young people in every field.

Levitt noted that his own career has crossed several countries and continents, and his Stanford research group included people from India, China, Europe and South America. He said science is international and that his work, kept on a computer, lets him work from anywhere, and he said he feels very at home in China. Looking ahead, he named stability and engagement with young people as priorities for the forum's future success in building international scientific collaboration. The article does not give details of any specific future events or plans beyond these priorities.

Articles.Title: AI offers answers, curiosity drives discovery - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: GT Economic Investigates: What does the Wuzhen summit reveal about China-US AI cooperation amid intensifying competition?
stories.Summary:
At the World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in East China's Zhejiang Province, held in early November 2026, Chinese and US artificial intelligence developers displayed their work side by side even as competition between them intensified. Debora Comparin, co-chair of an International Telecommunication Union initiative on trust and identity for humans and agentic AI, told the Global Times that constructive cooperation between the two countries was essential. Her remarks came just days after the US government ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and services from their IT systems and exclude them from procurement. Microsoft had already made the Chinese developer's R1 model available to customers through its Azure AI Foundry platform. Intel, Qualcomm and Microsoft were among the US companies exhibiting alongside Chinese firms at the Light of Internet Expo.

The competition is increasingly about price as well as performance. Stanford University's 2026 AI Index found that top US and Chinese models began trading places in performance rankings in early 2025, with the leading US model holding a 2.7 percent advantage in the Arena ratings as of March 2026. In September 2026, DeepSeek cut its API prices with the release of V4.1 Flash, a smaller model that added visual understanding. Its higher-end V4 Pro was priced at $3.96 per million output tokens, while Anthropic listed its flagship Claude Opus 5.5 at $20 per million output tokens. Government action has narrowed some choices, as an October 27 US Department of Energy notice described an order from the Department of Homeland Security excluding DeepSeek from federal civilian procurement.

A January 2026 US Commerce Department decision also said it would review licenses for certain advanced chip exports to China case by case. Those who spoke with the Global Times pointed to areas where cooperation remains possible. Comparin said Chinese and US companies could work with European partners on protocols and safeguards so that AI agents can operate securely across platforms. Intel showed enterprise AI workstations and PCs built to run AI agents, and said it was working with Chinese partners on uses such as visual quality inspection.

On October 5, Qualcomm and Huawei announced a multi-year agreement covering cross-licenses in 5G, computing, AI and networking, with Qualcomm also agreeing to buy certain Huawei US patents subject to regulatory approvals. In October, Amazon Web Services announced that Zhipu AI's GLM-5.3 was generally available on Amazon Bedrock. Chinese technology analyst Liu Dingding argued that such partnerships can help multinational companies commercialize technologies while supporting industrial upgrading in China. Analysts also see shared standards and open models as a route forward.

In October, the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation announced new projects, including OpenAI's Open Responses and Alibaba's OpenSandbox, which provides isolated environments for running agents. China's Ministry of Commerce said the two countries held their first dialogue on AI under their economic and trade consultation mechanism during the eighth round of talks in the US, where they reached several points of consensus. Terry Sweetser of the Asia Pacific Network Information Centre said open models could make AI more widely accessible, and Sri Lankan entrepreneur Lilan Dayananda said healthy competition could prevent technological monopolies. Both points suggest that the two countries are still weighing rivalry against the gains from working together.

Articles.Title: GT Economic Investigates: What does the Wuzhen summit reveal about China-US AI cooperation amid intensifying competition? - Global Times

stories.Headline: China expresses ‘serious concern’ over UK's unfounded ‘cyber challenge’ claims regarding Chinese AI; politicizing tech competition harms global AI governance: expert
stories.Summary:
China has voiced "grave concern" over claims by Britain's National Cyber Security Centre, part of the Government Communications Headquarters, that China is a leading developer of AI-enabled cyber capability. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the comments at a regular press briefing on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, when asked about reports that the agency said China would be "highly likely" by 2028 to routinely use AI-enabled hacking, posing the "most sophisticated and sustained" cyber challenge to the UK. Mao said the accusations were speculative and unsupported by evidence. She argued that Britain had long politicized cybersecurity and was reviving hacking allegations as a pretext to curb China's AI development. Beijing says such moves damage mutual trust and weaken the UK's credibility on global AI security governance.

Mao said AI-generated cyber risks are a global problem that calls for new rules formulated through the United Nations. She restated China's position that AI development should be open, aimed at progress and good for all, balancing security and advancement while remaining safe, reliable and controllable. A Huaqiao University professor, Hu Qimu, told the Global Times that linking China's rapid AI growth to cyber threats reflects a tendency to politicize technological competition, which could undermine cooperation on shared security challenges. Hu said China's expanding open-source AI ecosystem has created new opportunities for international technology cooperation. She warned that framing Chinese advances mainly as security threats could deepen mistrust and make common rules for safe AI development harder to reach.

China pointed to its recent efforts on AI governance as evidence of its approach. The Global AI Governance Action Plan was released in July 2025 at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, calling for stronger scientific and technological cooperation, better policy coordination and more support for developing countries. In July 2026, 29 countries signed an agreement in Shanghai to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry. Hu said addressing AI security challenges requires international cooperation and commonly accepted rules rather than geopolitical confrontation. The articles do not report any UK response to Beijing's remarks.

Articles.Title: China expresses ‘serious concern’ over UK's unfounded ‘cyber challenge’ claims regarding Chinese AI; politicizing tech competition harms global AI governance: expert - Global Times

stories.Headline: In Depth: Envision Tests New Model for Green AI Data Centers
stories.Summary:
Envision Group, a Chinese green technology company, has delivered the first 200-megawatt phase of an AI data center in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, in northern China. The project, called Galaxy Campus, was handed over to a Chinese internet giant in late October 2026, according to Zheng Zihao, general manager of Envision's AI data center business, who spoke to Caixin. A second 200-megawatt phase is expected to start operating in the second quarter of 2027. The project is meant to run on renewable power carried directly from nearby wind and solar farms. Envision plans to bring electricity from a company-built wind farm more than 100 kilometers away, which would meet roughly 80% of the campus's electricity demand.

The site uses three layers of energy storage, including a four-hour system near the wind farm, a 30-minute system on the campus, and a millisecond-response facility close to the GPUs. Envision also uses AI models to forecast power supply and demand over the next 15 minutes, and it expects the rate of abandoned electricity to stay below 10%. The article presents these details as Envision's own plans and results, and it does not give independent verification of them. Zheng described the design as a model for the broader industry, and the article reports that industrial power in Ulanqab costs roughly 0.32 to 0.35 yuan per kilowatt-hour. The city is a little more than 200 kilometers from Beijing and offers low network latency and a cool climate, which the article cites as further advantages of the location.

The wider policy backdrop is also part of the picture. As of September 2026, 24 Chinese provinces had issued policies supporting direct green-power connection projects, and 12 approved projects involved computing facilities. Ulanqab had signed contracts for 89 data center projects as of June 2026. The article does not describe any further steps beyond the second phase due in 2027.

Articles.Title: In Depth: Envision Tests New Model for Green AI Data Centers - Caixin Global

stories.Headline: 3 foreign nationals allegedly used AI to mimic CEOs in $129M scheme, DOJ says
stories.Summary:
Three foreign nationals have been charged in an alleged international fraud scheme that federal prosecutors say used AI to impersonate corporate executives and attorneys and steal more than $129 million. According to an indictment filed in the Southern District of New York, Jacob Soall was arrested in Spain in June, Sharon Hazan was arrested in Spain in August, and Guy Sheetrit was arrested in the United Kingdom in September. Prosecutors say the scheme ran from July 2024 to February 2026. The U.S. attorney's office says the group used the technology to copy the voices and images of company executives and attorneys at major law firms. The group allegedly targeted employees, typically in accounting departments, by telling them they were helping with a confidential financial transaction.

Using AI to mimic a chief executive's voice, the scheme then directed staff to contact supposed lawyers at large international law firms, who were in fact part of the operation. One participant would then instruct the employee to wire large sums to bank accounts set up around the world. The money was converted into cryptocurrency to hide its source and divided among the participants and their co-conspirators. Prosecutors allege the victims included an investment bank in New York, hospital systems in Missouri and California, a bank in Rhode Island, a financial technology company in the U.K., a mutual fund company in Massachusetts and a pet food company in Florida.

Prosecutors say Soall impersonated U.K. attorneys and used a script titled "Lawyer Call" to appear credible to victims. They also allege that Hazan handled laundering for the scheme and boasted that he had been doing so since 1994, claiming more than $400 million laundered in the past three years. Hazan was previously convicted of conspiracy to commit bank fraud in the same district in 2008. Sheetrit is also accused of laundering funds.

All three face charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, two counts of aggravated identity theft, money laundering conspiracy and two counts of money laundering, and each charge carries a maximum sentence of 20 years. U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said in the release that the technology offers large potential but that some people seek to use it for crime. He urged individuals and businesses to consider how to protect themselves from what he called the emerging threat of AI-enabled crime, using the abbreviation SI, which he noted is the White House's preferred term for artificial intelligence. The articles do not say whether the defendants have entered pleas or obtained lawyers, or when they might be tried or extradited to the United States.

Articles.Title: 3 foreign nationals allegedly used AI to mimic CEOs in $129M scheme, DOJ says

stories.Headline: Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate
stories.Summary:
Amazon's North America Sort Center planning teams, supported by an AWS-hosted team, have built a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI agents conversational access to the company's enterprise data lake. The server runs on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate and was described in an AWS article published on November 6, 2026. It was built to replace a pattern in which each AI agent wired itself directly to databases and APIs, duplicating integration logic and access control. The article presents the system as a centralized, agent-agnostic gateway between AI agents and the data lake.

The design is metadata-driven, so adding a dataset requires only a JSON metadata file that the server finds automatically on the next pipeline sync, with no custom integration code. The data lake holds thousands of datasets, and under the old model each new table could take several days of engineering work. The architecture is split into four layers covering the client, the MCP server, the tools, and knowledge-base refresh, each independently scalable. A metadata catalog stores schema descriptions, column semantics, and table relationships, which the agent consults at query time rather than relying on hardcoded table structures.

Access control is enforced in one place at the MCP server layer. The article credits the team that supports Amazon's North America Sort Center network, whose planning teams use operational data to manage capacity, labor, and package flow, with building the system. The authors describe the server as their answer to fragmented data access and an unsustainable onboarding model. They do not describe any outside reviews or external reactions to the work.

Requests move from client applications through Amazon Route 53 and an Application Load Balancer protected by AWS WAF, then through Amazon Cognito authentication, to the ECS Fargate services. Conversation state is kept in Amazon DynamoDB so that Fargate tasks can be replaced or scaled without losing data. The tools query Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift and use Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases for semantic search, with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails applied to model interactions. The article reports end-to-end interaction latency in the 15 to 20 second range in its testing, and it says that scoping queries to relevant tables through a context mapping configuration helps keep that latency there.

Articles.Title: Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate

stories.Headline: NTT Data plans further investment in Indonesian data centres amid rising AI and cloud demand
stories.Summary:
Japan's NTT Data Group plans to expand its data centre investments in Indonesia as demand for artificial intelligence and cloud computing grows across the region. The company has put USD 500 million into Indonesian data centres since 2015 and is considering the purchase of more land under a two-to-three-year expansion plan. Its expansion was announced alongside the opening of a 12-megawatt data centre annex in Jakarta. NTT Data has not said how much it will invest in the coming phase. The move comes as local concerns grow over electricity use, water supply, land use and opposition from some communities.

Yasuhiro Kajiki, managing director for Japan and Asia Pacific at NTT Data's data centre business, said the company is pursuing an aggressive expansion strategy in the country. He did not give a figure for future spending. The plan includes buying additional land and adding capacity for businesses that need computing infrastructure for AI, cloud services and other digital applications. The company has not said how many facilities it intends to build, where they will go, or when individual projects will start.

Market data suggests strong room for growth. A Research and Markets report published in January valued Indonesia's data centre market at USD 2.81 billion in 2025 and forecast it would reach USD 6.08 billion by 2031. That growth reflects rising use of cloud computing, digital platforms and AI services that need facilities to store and process large volumes of data. Operators must still secure suitable land, power and reliable connectivity before projects can proceed. Those requirements, along with community concerns, will shape how quickly the expansion moves forward.

Large data centres need substantial electricity to run servers and cooling systems, and some cooling technologies also use water. Competition for land and pressure on power networks have led to opposition against some projects in Indonesia and Malaysia. Kajiki said engaging with local communities is important and acknowledged that some developments face resistance from residents. The company's ability to secure sites and progress projects may therefore depend on how well it addresses those concerns as well as on commercial demand. It has not said how future Indonesian projects will handle energy and water use or whether it will set specific efficiency targets.

Articles.Title: NTT Data plans further investment in Indonesian data centres amid rising AI and cloud demand - Prop News Time

stories.Headline: Fearing AI disruption, white-collar workers are quitting their jobs
stories.Summary:
In November 2026, the Guardian reported that a growing number of white-collar workers are quitting their jobs out of fear that artificial intelligence will disrupt their careers. The article, written by Amelia Penniman, opened with the case of AI researcher Mrinank Sharma, who left his job at Anthropic earlier that year and warned in a widely shared resignation letter of a world in peril from the technology. Sharma said he was moving on and planned to study poetry. Other workers in tech, public relations, consulting and beyond have since made similar moves, saying AI changed the substance and stability of their jobs.

The article notes that no evidence yet links AI to mass layoffs. According to the Economist, AI has created about 1 million US jobs, compared with 200,000 layoffs attributed to it. Even so, 71 percent of Americans believe the technology will lead to fewer jobs over the next 20 years, according to a Pew Research Center survey. Among the people profiled, Vanessa Hsia, 30, left a decade in public relations for a master's degree in comparative literature, and Hanna Horvath, 29, left her editing job at Bankrate to freelance and work as a financial planner. Chris, a former software engineer, joined a major east coast city's police department, and Kara, an advertising producer, shifted toward acting.

The workers interviewed describe a range of reasons for leaving. Several said AI tools had been pushed on their teams, and some said that made the work feel meaningless or legally risky. Horvath wrote that the technology "has already changed worker psychology," and Kara described the job as having become untenable. The article also quotes Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who in May 2025 predicted AI would displace half of all entry-level white-collar jobs by the end of the decade, a prediction the article says has not yet materialized. Brendan Moore, an economics professor at the University of Notre Dame, said worker fears may stem partly from executives' warnings and from layoffs that some companies attribute to AI, though some of those cuts would likely have happened anyway.

Moore also warned that mass resignations driven by fear could affect the economy, much as the "great resignation" during the Covid-19 pandemic pushed wages and consumer inflation up. The article reports that Vermont senator Bernie Sanders introduced a bill to impose a federal moratorium on new AI datacenter construction until safeguards for displaced workers were in place. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, in an August essay, criticized the industry's doom-laden rhetoric. The article ends with workers describing the uncertainty as something they are now answering by taking control of their own careers.

Articles.Title: Fearing AI disruption, white-collar workers are quitting their jobs

stories.Headline: AI storm dooms tech stocks to biggest drop since Trump’s ‘Liberation Day’ rout
stories.Summary:
The Nasdaq Composite suffered its steepest one-day fall since "Liberation Day" in April 2025, dropping 5.5 per cent and erasing trillions of dollars in market value. Investors blamed a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections, which they feared could bring more scrutiny of artificial intelligence and slow the construction of data centres. The sell-off was the second straight session of heavy selling in AI stocks. The concern centres on whether the build-out of AI infrastructure can keep pace, since the midterm result raised the prospect of tougher oversight.

Smaller firms face particular pressure because higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions have already limited their ability to raise funds. The article links these pressures to a broader rethinking of the AI trade, which had been buoyant until recently. The Nasdaq has now posted five declines of more than 500 points since mid-October, a pattern the report ties to growing scrutiny of the AI trade over the past several weeks. Reuters, which the article credits, reported that the selling followed the election results rather than any single company announcement.

The article does not name a specific official or company that set off the decline. Market analysts and investors quoted in the coverage describe the fall as a reaction to uncertainty rather than a verdict on the sector's long-term prospects. The articles provide no detail on new regulations or legislation that would follow from the election. Whether the selling deepens or steadies will depend on what the new Congress does on AI and data centres, a matter the articles leave unresolved.

Articles.Title: AI storm dooms tech stocks to biggest drop since Trump’s ‘Liberation Day’ rout - SCMP

stories.Headline: Ocient Raises $100M Series C Funding to Advance AI Solutions for Petabyte-Scale Environments
stories.Summary:
Ocient, a Chicago-based data and analytics company, announced on November 5, 2026 that it had closed a $100 million Series C funding round. The round was co-led by BOKA Capital and OCA Ventures, with all existing investors participating, and it brings Ocient's total capital raised to $260 million. Several earlier backers joined the round, including Greycroft, In-Q-Tel, Blue Bear Capital, and Buoyant Ventures, while Dallas Venture Capital came in as a new investor. The company said the money will speed up delivery of its OcientAIQ Solutions for organizations running AI agents against large, constantly changing datasets.

The funding comes as Ocient expects to more than triple its revenue this year, driven by customers in industries that depend on high-volume, continuously growing data. The company describes its OcientAIQ Solutions as tailored to specific industries and built on its OcientAIQ Unified Data Platform, which handles governance and fast analysis. Ocient also said it has widened its partner network this year and formally set up its India operations and Ocient National Security Solutions as dedicated subsidiaries. The press release frames the platform's value around governance, since it enforces access, policy, and lineage controls on agent activity. It adds that analysis runs inside the engine rather than through a language model, so results can be reproduced and audited.

John Morris, Ocient's chief executive, said customers operate at a scale where the speed and reliability of an answer can carry serious consequences, and that the investment will help extend the reach of OcientAIQ to more customers. John James, chief executive of BOKA Capital, said turning advanced technology into dependable operational capability is now the key test in defense and national security, and that he expects to join the board. Jim Dugan, founding managing partner of OCA Ventures, said his firm first invested because it believed in the team's ability to tackle problems others had largely left unsolved. The release also cites Gartner's projection that worldwide IT spending will reach $7.35 trillion in 2027, up 15% from 2026, as organizations push to industrialize AI.

Articles.Title: Ocient Raises $100M Series C Funding to Advance AI Solutions for Petabyte-Scale Environments - HPCwire

stories.Headline: Together AI Compiler Cuts AI Engine Setup Time to 9 Seconds
stories.Summary:
Together AI introduced a compiler for AI inference workloads on November 4, 2026, saying it cut engine setup time from 467 seconds to nine seconds. The system can reload candidate GPU-code changes without restarting, according to the company. The compiler uses agents to rewrite GPU code and tests candidate changes through a two-tier system. Fast engines support quick iterations, while slower engines give more accurate measurements. The company says the approach raised experimentation throughput to 252 times the level of baseline agentic systems and that the compiler is now operational.

In tests completed in under 24 hours, throughput rose between 1.3 and 3 times across Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1-Flash and DeepSeek v4.1-Flash. On the InferenceX low-latency benchmark, the compiler reached 1,111 tokens per second on MiniMax M3.1-Flash and 1,205 tokens per second on DeepSeek v4.1-Flash. It also beat open-source megakernels by 1.7 times in a Llama 1B test with a batch size of one. Together AI is the party behind the announcement, and its figures come from its own testing. The company says its optimization system selects parallelism strategies using hardware specifications, microbenchmarks and real-world traffic data.

Its results are reported by TokenPost, which noted that inference performance can vary with the model, hardware and traffic patterns. The article also cites an overnight optimization that cut Phonic-1's median time to first speech by nearly 50 percent. Together AI says the compiler can also be applied to weather modeling, partial differential equations, time-series analysis and biology. The articles do not describe any further rollout plans or independent verification of the benchmark results. For now, the claims rest on the company's own tests and the figures it has published.

Articles.Title: Together AI Compiler Cuts AI Engine Setup Time to 9 Seconds - www.tokenpost.com

stories.Headline: Dataiku Headless Tackles a Growing Problem With AI Coding Agents
stories.Summary:
Dataiku has introduced Headless, a platform capability that lets developers use AI coding tools such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor to build and change data pipelines, models, dashboards, and agents while working inside Dataiku. The company first previewed the work in September with updates to Cobuild and has now shared how developers can use it and which coding tools it supports. The goal is to let developers keep working with their preferred assistants without moving the work outside a company's governed data environment. The connection runs through the Model Context Protocol, a standard that lets AI assistants interact with other software. Dataiku provides an MCP server with tools for its platform, along with instructions that help coding agents use them.

In Claude Code, users install a plugin and set up a connection to Dataiku, after which they can ask Claude to make changes to their projects without opening Dataiku each time. Headless can also convert older Excel spreadsheet reporting and Alteryx workflows into the platform, and it can update existing pipelines or help diagnose why a workflow is not producing expected results. Dataiku is the company behind the announcement, and its executives frame the product as a way to bring AI-generated code under management, since code produced by agents often ends up scattered across development environments that others find hard to understand or reuse. The company says the approach keeps permissions, dependencies, and access rules intact, which a working script alone does not guarantee. The articles note that data engineers would still need to check the output, especially when other teams rely on the pipelines.

The release is part of Dataiku 15.1, which also adds Cobuild Insights for asking questions about company data, Agent Management for tracking AI agents including those built on other platforms, and a larger catalog of reusable assets. Support for Snowflake CoCo is included, and developers can find the MCP server and supporting skills on GitHub. Dataiku has not shared pricing or commercial availability terms. How well the tool handles larger or more complicated legacy migrations will become clearer as customers test it.

Articles.Title: Dataiku Headless Tackles a Growing Problem With AI Coding Agents - HPCwire

stories.Headline: MariaDB Introduces Enterprise Platform 2027 with New AI Tools
stories.Summary:
MariaDB plc announced MariaDB Enterprise Platform 2027 on November 4, 2026, in a release that the company says brings 56% higher peak throughput, stronger resilience for multi-region deployments and new tools for building and running AI agents. The platform combines transactional, analytical, in-memory, AI and multi-region capabilities on one foundation, and it arrives alongside a new brand identity meant to show the company's shift from a database vendor to a platform. The company's stated aim is to help enterprises add AI agents to existing systems rather than building an extra layer for them. The release is described as generally available that day.

The new tools include AI Retrieval, which grounds agents in documents and live operational data and turns natural-language questions into read-only SQL, and AI plugins for coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Agent Memory provides a durable in-memory store shared across sessions, while Semantic Cache returns stored answers to questions asked in different words. MariaDB Exa runs real-time analytics on live data, and vector search is built into the core engine, delivering up to 30% more queries per second than the last major release. Scaling features include Raft clustering and conflict detection and resolution for multi-region deployments, and security features include unified role-based access controls, Bring Your Own Cloud and FIPS 140-3 support. AI Retrieval is slated for public preview on MariaDB Cloud later in November.

Rohit de Souza, CEO of MariaDB plc, said the AI race will be won by companies that unify their infrastructure beneath their agents, and that the company has moved well beyond being just a database. Tracy Strauss, the company's CMO, described the new brand identity, with its redesigned logo and bolder visual system, as reflecting a company that is open by design and built for the agentic enterprise. Analysts quoted in the release, Devin Pratt of IDC and Sanjeev Mohan of SanjMo, argued that building agent capabilities on a proven transactional core is a more durable approach than starting from analytics. The release cites IDC predictions that agent use among the world's 2,000 largest companies will rise tenfold by 2027 and that firms lacking AI-ready data foundations will face a 15% productivity loss. A webinar on the platform is scheduled for November 18, 2026.

Articles.Title: MariaDB Introduces Enterprise Platform 2027 with New AI Tools - HPCwire

stories.Headline: Cohere Details Canadian Investment in AI Research and Infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Cohere, the AI company founded in Toronto, shared an update on November 4, 2026 about its investments in Canada and announced new commitments to expand its presence there. The multi-year effort, which began in 2024, is now expected to create more than 1,500 jobs and deliver more than C$4 billion in research and development and AI infrastructure investment through 2031. About 1,000 of those roles are expected to focus on AI research, engineering, product development and other advanced technical fields. The company says the commitment is meant to build Canada's capacity to develop and deploy advanced AI, and to anchor its next phase of global growth in the country.

Under the commitment, Cohere expects to invest in research and infrastructure across multiple provinces between 2024 and 2031, supporting domestic innovation and what it calls sovereign AI capabilities. It also plans to offer more than 250 paid student roles by 2029, giving students hands-on experience with AI work. The company is building a national network of university and research partnerships, beginning with recently announced collaborations with the University of Toronto and the University of Waterloo. It says it will also build on existing relationships with Amii, Vector and Mila to link Canadian research and talent with real-world AI adoption. Cohere describes these steps as part of a broader effort to turn Canadian research into products, businesses and jobs.

Cohere presented the commitment as a response to a gap it sees in Canada's AI sector, where strong research does not always become commercial products or local jobs. The company argues that building an AI business requires access to talent, infrastructure and market opportunities, and that without them Canadian firms and workers may look elsewhere to grow. It also ties the announcement to the goals of Canada's national AI strategy, which aims to raise GDP by 3% and create up to 250,000 AI-related jobs by 2031. According to the article, only 12% of Canadian businesses reported using AI to produce goods or deliver services in 2025, and the Bank of Canada has identified wider adoption as a key route to higher productivity and wages. Cohere says it hopes to help more Canadian organizations move AI from experimentation into full production use.

Articles.Title: Cohere Details Canadian Investment in AI Research and Infrastructure - HPCwire

stories.Headline: E2E Networks Plans 5.4 MW NVIDIA Blackwell AI Expansion in India
stories.Summary:
E2E Networks announced plans to add 5.4 megawatts of AI computing capacity in India, using NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture. The company said the addition would raise its total AI infrastructure to about 14.6 MW, an increase of nearly 59 percent. The expansion will include NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other Blackwell GPUs. The announcement was reported on October 28, 2026.

The new capacity is intended for foundation model training, post-training, production inference, agentic AI and multimodal applications. E2E Networks said demand is coming from higher education institutions, research organisations, foundation model developers, AI-native startups, enterprises and public-sector programmes. The company also plans to offer infrastructure hosted within India for customers whose data must stay under domestic jurisdiction, including regulated and data-sensitive environments. E2E Networks has not disclosed when the infrastructure will be commissioned, the capital expenditure planned, or the total number of GPUs to be deployed.

Tarun Dua, founder and managing director of E2E Networks, said Indian AI developers are moving beyond pilot-stage deployments and increasingly need infrastructure for production-scale workloads. He said customers also need infrastructure operating within their organisational boundaries to help protect data in line with national laws. On October 30, 2026, shares of E2E Networks hit their 5 percent lower circuit limit amid a global sell-off in technology stocks. Investors were concerned about rising spending on AI infrastructure, returns from those investments and rising borrowing costs, while earnings growth has failed to match the scale of investments.

The sell-off followed earnings announcements from major companies including Amazon.com and Intel, and Alphabet shares posted a record decline after its results. Jai Malhi, a senior equity strategist at Vanda Research, told Bloomberg that tech earnings have proven a major hurdle with investors becoming capex vigilantes, and that tech names are being punished if revenue growth does not beat a high bar given higher funding costs. Other AI-related Indian shares also fell, including Netweb Technologies, MTAR Technologies, Black Box, ESDS Software Solution, Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova T&D India, CG Power and Industrial Solutions and Anant Raj. In the US, chipmakers Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices fell 2.8 percent and 6.9 percent respectively in premarket trading.

Articles.Title: Nasdaq crashes 3%: E2E Networks, ESDS Software, other AI-related shares fall up to 5% - TradingView
