The natural-language prompt is run against each batch in parallel through Vertex AI, and the intermediate summaries are then combined and passed back to the model with the same instruction until one final string remains for each GROUP BY group. The article says the function uses full-weight LLMs at every stage, unlike row-level functions that can use distilled proxy models. It also supports multimodal inputs through object tables and OBJ.GET_ACCESS_URL, and it works within VPC Service Controls. Several operating limits are listed: each group's output is capped at 10,000 tokens, each row must stay under 10 MiB, rows with fewer than 10 images are recommended, and queries should handle no more than 20 million rows and 1,000 distinct groups.

Pramod Niralakeri presents the function as a way to turn the data warehouse into an active system for semantic analysis, and the post recommends practices for production use. Those include wrapping nullable struct fields in IFNULL, because a single null field causes the whole row to be discarded, and writing prompts as strict output contracts. The article also advises using WHERE and LIMIT filters to control costs, since recursive batching sends more tokens to Gemini than the source data contains, and it suggests using AI.COUNT_TOKENS to estimate costs before running a query. Examples in the post include summarizing forum authors' comments, grouping critical logs by time window to surface root causes, and creating labels that feed into AI.CLASSIFY. The article does not report any customer adoption figures or release dates beyond the preview status.

Articles.Title: Semantic data aggregation with BigQuery and AI.AGG

stories.Headline: Stocks crater as investors recoil from tech companies amid AI risks
stories.Summary:
Stocks fell sharply on Thursday as investors pulled back from technology companies tied to artificial intelligence, according to CBS MoneyWatch reporter Mary Cunningham. The sell-off was driven by concern that a shift in congressional control after the U.S. midterm elections could slow the construction of data centers that power AI services. Market watchers said the Democrats' sweeping electoral wins this week could strengthen opponents of those facilities, which have faced widespread public opposition. The broader market was hit across the board, but technology stocks suffered the worst losses.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index fell 1,285 points, or 5%, in early-afternoon trading. The S&P 500 dropped 287 points, or 3.7%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 1,542 points, or 2.9%. Chip makers and other AI-exposed firms took the hardest hits, with Nvidia shares down 7.5% after a 3.2% drop the day before. Advanced Micro Devices fell 14.6%, while CoreWeave, which rents access to AI chips over the cloud, dropped 12.1%. Wall Street analyst Adam Crisafulli of Vital Knowledge described the moves as a sign that investors are reacting to growing headline risks around AI.

Oil markets showed a different pattern, with the initial reaction to the election results fading somewhat. The price of a barrel of Brent crude rose 2.6% to $97.11, recovering much of the nearly 9% drop from the previous day. The article notes that uncertainty remains about the war with Iran and about when the global energy industry can return to normal. It does not say how long the volatility in either market is expected to last.

Articles.Title: Stocks crater as investors recoil from tech companies amid AI risks

stories.Headline: OpenAI debuts new cybersecurity-focused AI model amid growing alarm about AI-driven cyber attacks
stories.Summary:
OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a new artificial intelligence model built for cybersecurity professionals, according to a November 5, 2026 report by Fortune. The company says the model performs better than its general-purpose GPT-6 Astra model on most cyber tasks. Because the model could be misused to carry out cyberattacks, OpenAI is making it available only to a small group of approved security customers for now. The release comes as AI tools grow better at finding software flaws and turning them into working attacks.

The articles describe the model's focus as advanced vulnerability research and exploit development, the kind of work that tests whether a system can be broken into. OpenAI tested it on Firefox and the Linux kernel, where the company says researchers found 81 previously unknown, high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities. The company also says researchers developed working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including 588 flaws not previously known, and some of these could let an attacker gain the highest level of control over a system. Initial access is limited to approved Daybreak Red customers, with access expanding to all Red customers over the coming weeks.

Gartner forecast in September that worldwide spending on AI cybersecurity would reach $51.3 billion this year, nearly double last year's $25.9 billion. OpenAI describes this as a market it is increasingly pursuing to grow its enterprise sales, and it has hired Dali Rajic, who comes from a cybersecurity software background, as chief revenue officer. The article notes this is OpenAI's fourth cybersecurity-focused model this year, following releases in April, June and August. Competitors Google and Anthropic are also courting security customers through vetted-access programs.

The articles note that the same techniques used to test defenses can be used in real attacks, which is why general-purpose models restrict some work that can also block legitimate security research. OpenAI has said its cyber models are trained both to improve specialized security skills and to reduce refusals on certain tasks. Fortune first reported in September that OpenAI was planning a specialized cyber model based on GPT-6. Beyond the initial rollout, the articles do not describe further planned steps.

Articles.Title: OpenAI debuts new cybersecurity-focused AI model amid growing alarm about AI-driven cyber attacks

stories.Headline: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics
stories.Summary:
Axiom Math, a startup valued at $1.6 billion, announced on Wednesday that it had formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the largest bodies of mathematics written by humans. The company's fleet of AI agents translated the library's roughly 7,654 pages into about 16 million lines of computer-checked code. The work was done in Lean, a programming language, and a proof assistant checks each line so that a passing proof can be trusted as logically sound. Axiom was founded in March 2025 by CEO Carina Hong, who had left a Stanford math Ph.D. program, and the company raised a $200 million Series A in March.

The Stacks Project was started in 2005 by Johan de Jong, a Columbia mathematician, as an open-source reference that others have added to over the years. Its theorems are tightly interconnected, so the team had to keep every connection intact across the entire translation. Ashvin Swaminathan, a member of Axiom's technical staff, said the agents worked in parallel, found their own tasks and were given only a loose hierarchy. Axiom also trained its own models to be strong at math, and an in-house Lean expert initially taught the agents a sense of taste before they picked it up on their own. The company says the result fills a large gap in formalized math in algebraic geometry.

Hong told TechCrunch that she was not sure vibe coding could preserve the beauty of the project, and she described the challenge as bringing together things that are big and things that are delicate. Swaminathan said that researchers working on algebraic geometry now have a verified base to build on. Terence Tao, a UCLA mathematician and Fields Medal winner, has argued that the more formalized proofs exist, the more can be made. Hong also issued an open challenge to other coding companies to work on formalization at this scale.

The effort is aimed at a wider concern about AI-generated work, as OpenAI recently released 719 manuscripts claiming solutions to hard problems and computer checks can themselves slip. Axiom's position is that verified foundations will matter for software as AI agents write more of the world's code, and that mathematics is a good place to start. Swaminathan said the agents can read, understand and build new infrastructure on top of the Lean formalization. Hong argued that agents need a reusable, well-built body of knowledge to avoid producing slop and to keep pushing the frontier.

Articles.Title: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics

stories.Headline: Redefining Investment Advisory in the Age of AI
stories.Summary:
On 2 November 2026, Forthright Securities, a Hong Kong brokerage under JF SmartInvest Holdings, took part in the Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK event at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre as a first-time exhibitor and Gold Sponsor. The company's pitch was that as its AI tools grow more capable, its human advisers matter more. The article is a paid post produced by the advertising partner, published on 5 November 2026, and the event opened on 2 November with more than 45,000 participants from over 120 economies. Regulators used the week to announce new measures on artificial intelligence applications and governance, tokenisation and payment connectivity.

The company's main product is the Forthright Smart Investment Terminal, a tablet aimed at experienced individual investors. It combines AI-powered analysis, real-time market support monitoring and analytical tools with the firm's investment research, while the human adviser handles questions the models cannot settle. The firm says its three most-used AI features, AI Assistant, Market Monitoring and Portfolio Analysis, have each been used by more than 80 per cent of clients. On the opening day, the Securities and Futures Commission set out plans for principles-based guidance on AI applications with greater autonomy, focused on safety and preserving human accountability and oversight.

Richard Zhengwei He, chief executive of Forthright Financial and Forthright Securities, spoke at a session titled "Agentic Alpha: The Future of Dynamic Wealth." He said agentic AI is goal-based and expects it to change how financial institutions work with clients in the short term. In the longer term, he said he sees no inherent conflict between financial institutions and agentic AI, which he described as bringing reliable, understandable and suitable guidance to people previously excluded from the financial system. Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee, speaking at the opening session, said the city has become the world's largest cross-boundary wealth hub, with net inflows to its asset and wealth management industry up roughly 200 per cent last year.

The article describes the wider context as a shift in how Hong Kong investors trade, with 95 per cent of the city's stock investors now trading online, according to the Investor and Financial Education Council's latest study. The company describes itself as a licensed brokerage that opened a four-floor flagship investor experience hub in Sheung Wan in July 2026 and gained virtual asset business qualifications in May 2026. The article does not say what the firm plans next beyond continuing to pair its AI tools with advisers. The text is promotional and carries a risk warning stating that AI analyses are for reference only and do not constitute investment advice.

Articles.Title: Redefining Investment Advisory in the Age of AI

stories.Headline: MCSO: Man arrested on child pornography charges following AI cyber tips
stories.Summary:
A Mobile man has been arrested on child pornography charges after an investigation sparked by artificial intelligence cyber tips, according to the Mobile County Sheriff's Office. Detectives executed a search warrant at a residence on Wellesley Court, where Daniel Thomas Gunn was taken into custody. The Internet Crimes Against Children Unit carried out the operation with help from the Special Operations Unit. The case opened after three cyber tip reports reached the sheriff's office from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Those reports came from the AI platform xAI, known as Grok, and concerned suspected child sexual abuse material.

Gunn, 47, faces five counts of unlawful production of child pornography and five counts of unlawful possession of child pornography, jail records show. He was booked into the Mobile County Metro Jail on Thursday morning. The charges reflect the number of counts filed so far, and the articles do not describe any other conditions attached to his booking. The articles give no details about bond or a court date. Nothing in the reports indicates whether additional charges are being considered.

The sheriff's office is the agency leading the case, and it is the source for the account of the warrant and the tips. The National Center for Missing and Exploited Children forwarded the three tip reports that started the investigation. The articles do not include any statement from Gunn, his attorney, or xAI about the allegations. The case shows how reports generated or flagged by AI platforms can lead to local criminal investigations of child sexual exploitation. The articles do not say what will happen next in the case, including whether Gunn will enter a plea or when any hearing will take place.

Articles.Title: MCSO: Man arrested on child pornography charges following AI cyber tips

stories.Headline: Florio: AI could speed building permits and ease local government costs on Long Island
stories.Summary:
Michael Florio, CEO of the Long Island Builders Institute, has argued in a Long Island Business News opinion column published November 5, 2026, that artificial intelligence could speed up building permit reviews and help local governments on Long Island manage rising costs. He describes two pressures: a housing affordability problem and the growing expense of running towns and villages. Permit applications often sit for weeks or months, and experienced building department staff are retiring without easy replacements. He says the cost of salaries, health care and pensions keeps climbing while towns operate under New York's property tax cap.

Florio proposes using AI-assisted tools to check applications for completeness, screen plans against building codes and give applicants preliminary feedback within hours or days rather than weeks. He stresses that this would not eliminate municipal employees or weaken public safety, since officials would keep responsibility for complex reviews, field inspections, compliance, audits and enforcement. Faster approvals, he argues, could reduce overtime, limit future staffing costs and bring new properties onto tax rolls sooner. He says this could grow municipal revenue without simply raising taxes on existing homeowners.

Florio calls on New York State to act, pointing to Governor Hochul's Pro-Housing Communities Program, which already offers financial incentives for communities addressing the housing shortage. He proposes a dedicated AI permitting pilot program that would offer grants to certified Pro-Housing Communities willing to modernize their building departments. Under his plan, the funding would help towns adopt AI-assisted plan review, train staff and evaluate the technology without adding burdens for local taxpayers. Participating communities would measure reductions in processing times, administrative costs and application backlogs while keeping safety standards and human oversight in place.

Florio acknowledges that AI cannot replace sound zoning, environmental protections or professional judgment. He nonetheless argues that legitimate concerns about new technology should not serve as reasons to keep outdated systems. The column presents the proposal as a practical partnership between state and local government, and it does not describe any adopted policy or scheduled pilot. The article itself does not report any response from state officials or the outcome of such a program.

Articles.Title: Florio: AI could speed building permits and ease local government costs on Long Island

stories.Headline: Box CEO Aaron Levie: Seeing continued acceleration with AI adoption
stories.Summary:
Box CEO Aaron Levie appeared on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on November 5, 2026, to discuss his company's latest partnership with Nvidia and the broader adoption of artificial intelligence. According to the segment description, Levie spoke about the company's new tie-up with the chipmaker and the wider trend of businesses taking up AI tools. The interview ran a little under four minutes and was posted to CNBC's website that same morning. The clip was one of several recent segments on the network's site touching on AI, including a discussion of a tech stock sell-off. The articles give few specifics about the partnership itself, so the terms, scope, and financial details of the Nvidia arrangement are not described.

Nothing in the available text states a figure, a timeline for new products, or a date when the partnership takes effect. The page does not say what changes for Box customers or how the collaboration would be implemented. Readers looking for those details will need the full interview or Box's own announcement. Levie is the chief executive of Box, the cloud content management company, and he is the sole voice quoted in the material provided. The segment description characterizes him as seeing continued acceleration in AI adoption, though the full remarks are not reproduced in the text.

The article does not include his exact words beyond that summary. Nvidia's position on the partnership is not reported in these articles. The surrounding coverage suggests AI remains a central topic for investors and executives, with other segments on the page addressing tech stock moves and AI's role in professional work. The articles do not say whether the Nvidia partnership will be expanded, announced in further detail, or followed by additional deals. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Box CEO Aaron Levie: Seeing continued acceleration with AI adoption

stories.Headline: Grimes is going to star in an AI movie that’s coming to theaters
stories.Summary:
Pop star Grimes will appear in Gods Don't Give Gifts, an AI-generated sci-fi anthology billed as the first AI film to come to theaters. The movie releases on December 4th, and Grimes is lending both her likeness and her vocal performance to it. The film's producer, AI studio Fable, announced the casting in a press release. The Verge reported the news on November 5, 2026. The project is being directed by Jack London, who is better known online as Gossip Goblin.

The anthology is set in a future where bodies are disposable and consciousness has been commoditized, following four interconnected stories about humanity's attempt to transcend the flesh. Those themes align with Grimes's past work, which has explored transhumanism and artificial intelligence. She is also working on an AI-themed album called Psy Opera. Fable's press release argued that casting an actor's likeness together with their spoken vocal performance will become more common in animated films using AI. The studio said audiences will increasingly see actors, athletes and musicians giving vocal performances with their likeness in films.

The Verge's Andrew Webster noted that Grimes's involvement could give the project some legitimacy as a test case for the commercial potential of AI films. The article places the film against a broader debate about AI in Hollywood. Despite plenty of hype, the author writes that no project has yet shown that the technology is a vital storytelling tool. Earlier AI efforts, including two takes on The Odyssey, one made with Elon Musk's Grok, left much to be desired. The article does not say how Gods Don't Give Gifts will be received once it reaches theaters.

Articles.Title: Grimes is going to star in an AI movie that’s coming to theaters

stories.Headline: Nasdaq plunges into correction territory as Dem wins threaten data centers — and AI giants rush to stem fallout
stories.Summary:
The Nasdaq fell 5.1% on Thursday, entering correction territory, as investors and industry leaders reacted to the Democrats' midterm sweep. Investors feared the new Congress would slow data-center projects and hit revenue at leading AI labs. The Dow dropped 1,097 points, or 2.1%, a day after recording its best session in 18 months, and the S&P 500 fell 3.2%. Neocloud firms such as CoreWeave and Nebius dropped 14.6% and 18%, while data-center operators Iren and Applied Digital fell 20% and 19.7%.

OpenAI responded on Thursday by releasing a "National Community Compact," a stricter framework for building data centers. The pledges include reducing power use during peak times, sharing data on noise, water and energy impacts, and making sure local residents do not pay higher electricity costs. The company also promised to publicly release construction plans, limit non-disclosure agreements for local officials, and set local hiring goals for nearby towns. Voters in 50 referendums related to data centers on Tuesday rejected new sites in at least 46 cases.

Meta President Dina Powell McCormick said on Wednesday that data centers were central to the Democratic results in exit polls, and she admitted that buildouts are "going to be harder" going forward. She said the opposition could be so large that hyperscalers consider building outside the United States. Analyst Dan Ives wrote that growth into 2028 will likely moderate significantly given the political map, especially in Texas, which holds roughly 26% of planned data-center capacity. UBS analysts estimated that construction pauses could affect around 30% of planned data-center capacity in 2028.

The sell-off came after the Nasdaq had set a record in October and then dropped more than 10% from that peak. OpenAI said it had worked on the Compact for months before the election results, and its chief global affairs officer said the company had spoken with residents, officials and candidates in Georgia, Ohio and Texas. Powell McCormick noted that at least one incoming governor who campaigned against data centers had expressed interest in meeting, because they did not want to lose the investment and its jobs. The articles do not say how markets will move from here.

Articles.Title: Nasdaq plunges into correction territory as Dem wins threaten data centers — and AI giants rush to stem fallout

stories.Headline: AMD CEO Lisa Su sees AI becoming 'essential to every aspect of our lives'
stories.Summary:
AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a Thursday interview on Sozzi Unleashed that she sees artificial intelligence becoming essential to nearly every part of life and business, even as investors grow nervous about whether AI demand will hold up. She described the market as sometimes short-sighted and said she is focused on the years ahead rather than near-term swings. Her comments came as AMD shares fell about 14% midday Thursday after rising 1% in the prior session. The stock has still gained roughly 128% so far this year. The remarks followed AMD's third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday evening, which beat expectations on both revenue and profit.

Quarterly sales rose 45% from a year earlier to a record $13.38 billion, above Wall Street estimates of about $13.06 billion. Adjusted earnings climbed 74% to $2.09 per share, compared with analyst projections of $1.94. The company's Data Center segment led the gains, with revenue up 97% to a record $8.5 billion on demand for its EPYC server processors and the ramp of its Instinct MI450 AI accelerators. Su said she believes computing equates to intelligence, so the more compute a company has, the more problems it can solve and the faster it can grow. She argued that companies must invest now for a horizon of three to five years and beyond.

For the fourth quarter, AMD said it expects data center revenue to grow 50% sequentially. For 2027, Su guided to revenue growth of more than 80%, with server revenue doubling and data center AI more than doubling. Citi analyst Atif Malik said that with AMD's AI business reaching what he called escape velocity, investor focus is shifting from proving competitiveness to executing a multiyear ramp built around the MI450 and MI455 accelerators, the Helios and Venice platforms, and significant operating leverage as the business scales. The articles do not indicate what further steps, if any, AMD or analysts plan beyond these projections.

Articles.Title: AMD CEO Lisa Su sees AI becoming 'essential to every aspect of our lives'

stories.Headline: AI architecture gaps keep agents stuck in demo mode
stories.Summary:
Oracle executive Çetin Özbütün, speaking with theCUBE Research's Dave Vellante at Oracle AI World, said that most companies can build a convincing AI agent demo but struggle to move agents into production. He said nearly 70% of organizations plan to deploy AI agents, yet very few have done so. The interview was broadcast live on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media's livestreaming studio, and covered the architecture problems that keep agents stuck at the demonstration stage. Özbütün framed the issue as four separate deployment difficulties that enterprises typically run into.

The first difficulty he named is security, since giving AI agents secure access to data is hard and ranks among the top challenges. He said agents are finding vulnerabilities at unprecedented rates and customers often cannot patch their databases before attackers exploit them. Oracle's Autonomous AI Database encrypts data at rest and in transit by default, and users cannot turn those protections off. On resiliency, Oracle commits to 99.995% availability with no exclusions, measured by whether a client can connect and run queries. Özbütün said Oracle patches its systems weekly using online patches, so the database keeps accepting connections during updates.

Özbütün also said the database enforces the security profiles customers define under Oracle's Deep Trust AI architecture, and that new capabilities such as the expanded Deep Data Security features appear in Autonomous AI Database as soon as they are announced, ahead of on-premises releases. He said users do nothing to receive these functions, which become available on day one. The interview was part of SiliconANGLE's and theCUBE's coverage at Oracle AI World. The article notes that theCUBE is a paid media partner for the event, and that neither Oracle nor other sponsors have editorial control over its content.

Articles.Title: AI architecture gaps keep agents stuck in demo mode

stories.Headline: New communication and memory tools reduce AI data traffic and response delays
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Seoul National University, led by professor Kyunghan Lee, have developed two technologies aimed at easing AI data traffic and response delays on smartphones. One, called TACToC, is a communication system that sends only the information an AI task needs, and the other, mzCache, is a memory management system that shortens the wait when a user returns to an AI app after using others. Both papers were accepted for ACM MobiCom 2026, a mobile computing and networking conference held in Austin, Texas, from October 26 to 30. TACToC reportedly cut communication costs by up to 14.5 times compared with existing methods while keeping the accuracy loss within 3 percentage points. In multi-app settings, mzCache reduced the time to first response by up to 5.5 times compared with conventional storage-based recovery.

TACToC replaces the usual practice of training a separate encoder for each AI task with a single encoder that selects only the visual features a given task requires. New tasks can be added by training a small set of task tokens, which the researchers said takes only about 1,900 parameters and roughly 12.5 milliseconds to switch. In tests on public datasets covering five tasks, including semantic segmentation, pose estimation and image captioning, communication costs fell by 1.5 to 14.5 times. The system also reduced bandwidth use by about 16.7 percent compared with H.265 video compression and about 41.1 percent compared with an existing task-oriented method. The team said it can be deployed without changing existing communication network architectures, making it relevant to autonomous vehicles, robots, drones and intelligent CCTV.

The problem mzCache addresses arises when the operating system reclaims memory held by an on-device AI model after a user switches to another app such as a camera or game. In the team's measurements on real smartphones, the time to first response rose from 0.8 seconds to about 16 seconds after the user returned to the AI. When memory pressure grew severe, the AI could be forcibly terminated and its conversation context lost. mzCache divides AI memory into small units so it reclaims only what other apps need, then restores data while the GPU computes on what is already available. On phones including the Galaxy S25+ and OnePlus 12, it cut response time by 2.1 to 5.5 times against conventional methods, and in a 45-minute test switching among 10 apps, the AI stayed active through 10 repeated trials.

The research was led by Huijeong Choe with colleagues at KAIST for TACToC, and by Hongseung Yu, a master's student, with colleagues for mzCache, with Professor Lee serving as corresponding author on both papers. Professor Lee said the TACToC work establishes a technical foundation for network-based physical AI, while the mzCache work supports responsive, context-preserving on-device AI even under limited memory. The team plans to extend both technologies to settings where several AI applications run at once and to a wider range of mobile processors, including neural processing units. The article does not give a release date for either technology in commercial products.

Articles.Title: New communication and memory tools reduce AI data traffic and response delays

stories.Headline: El-Erian Says Stock Market Is ‘Overdoing It’ On AI Fears As Nasdaq Enters Correction Territory
stories.Summary:
On Thursday, November 5, 2026, U.S. stock markets fell sharply in midday trading, with the Nasdaq dropping 4.2% and putting it on track for its worst session since April 2025. The decline pushed the Nasdaq more than 10% below the record it reached last month, placing it in correction territory. The S&P 500 fell more than 3%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,153 points. The selloff came the day after a rally, and it was focused on artificial intelligence-related stocks.

AI-linked shares took the heaviest losses. Nvidia fell more than 7%, reaching levels last seen in April, while SanDisk dropped more than 17% and Nebius slid 16.7%, also hitting April lows. Micron and AMD declined more than 13% and 15% respectively, both reaching lows last seen in May. The leveraged semiconductor ETF SOXL plunged more than 30%, putting it on track for its biggest one-day decline since April 2025. The article reports that these moves followed the midterm elections, which handed Democrats control of both chambers of Congress, and that investors are waiting to see how AI and data center build-out will shape up afterward.

Mohamed El-Erian, chief economic adviser at Allianz, spoke to CNBC and said the growing public backlash against artificial intelligence is a warning the U.S. should heed, though he believes investors are overreacting to it. He argued the industry has not done enough to explain how AI could affect jobs and daily life, and he compared the situation to globalization, which he said suffered a backlash after distributional effects were ignored. He said he remains completely bullish on AI's potential to benefit the economy, while warning that the U.S. economy is really levered on AI, so a sharp tech selloff could spill into the wider economy. He also expects the 10-year Treasury yield to stay around 5% unless a recession occurs, and he thinks the Federal Reserve will raise rates at least once more, though not the three hikes markets are pricing in.

Articles.Title: El-Erian Says Stock Market Is ‘Overdoing It’ On AI Fears As Nasdaq Enters Correction Territory

stories.Headline: ElevenLabs now lets users publish AI-generated music directly on SoundCloud
stories.Summary:
ElevenLabs said on Thursday, November 5, 2026, that users can now publish AI-generated music made with its ElevenMusic platform directly on SoundCloud. The company announced the change as part of a broader push to bring its tools into the streaming world. SoundCloud is also offering its Artist Pro subscribers three months of ElevenMusic Pro as a bonus. That package lets users generate up to 1,000 songs, split song stem files 500 times, and create five custom styles or vocals per month.

ElevenLabs first released a music-generation model in 2025 and followed with a consumer app in April 2026 that creates songs from written prompts. A month later it released a newer model able to switch genres mid-track and handle more complex vocals. The company said users have created more than 25 million tracks with its models so far. SoundCloud has taken a different route with AI, having recently partnered with the music tooling company Moises so artists can move songs to and from the platform. It also has integrations with other services, including Google Flow Music and the remix platform Hook.

SoundCloud CEO Eliah Seton described the move in a statement as a way to give artists room to experiment and reach audiences beyond SoundCloud's own ecosystem. He said the platform is the first to bring ElevenMusic creations directly to fans in that way. ElevenLabs also has a separate partnership with Spotify, under which authors can use its audio models to create audiobook narrations and publish them there. The article notes that Spotify has not yet named a model partner like ElevenLabs for its AI remixing products, even though it has signed label deals for them.

The article places the announcement against a wider trend in which other streaming platforms are moving to label or filter AI-generated music. Deezer is adding a toggle that lets listeners filter out AI music entirely, and Bandcamp has banned AI-generated tracks outright. Spotify and YouTube have taken a more cautious approach to labeling. The article does not say how SoundCloud will label or filter ElevenLabs tracks once they are uploaded.

Articles.Title: ElevenLabs now lets users publish AI-generated music directly on SoundCloud

stories.Headline: Home-based patient care among AI applications being tested at next-gen 5G, 6G research centre
stories.Summary:
On November 3, 2026, the National University Health System (NUHS), telco Singtel and telecommunications equipment maker Ericsson signed a memorandum of understanding to open a research centre testing AI healthcare on 5G-Advanced and 6G networks. The centre is exploring a future in which hospital patients recovering at home are watched by wearable medical devices that detect dangerous changes, such as a sudden spike in blood pressure or an abnormal heart rate. If the readings point to an emergency, hospital staff and emergency services are alerted in real time. NUHS chief executive Yeoh Khay Guan said the partners hope to turn future telecommunications technology into practical healthcare applications. NUHS runs hospitals including National University Hospital, Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and Alexandra Hospital.

The partners say current 5G may not cope with the larger data loads expected as more patients recover at home, patient data becomes more complex and AI tools generate more data. The newer networks are expected to handle those volumes, with 5G-Advanced launched in 2025 and 6G slated for commercial launch in 2030. According to Singtel, the newer networks will be faster than current 5G and have much lower latency, meaning they respond more quickly. Chau Yuen, an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University, said 6G is predicted to support a much larger number of connected devices. Because more processing can move to the cloud, devices such as augmented reality headsets could be made smaller and less bulky.

Yeoh said the planned uses include autonomous mobile robots for logistics and patient care, internet-connected devices for home care and support for surgeons during operations. NUHS plans to replace its Microsoft HoloLens headsets, which surgeons use to view a holographic image of a patient's heart from CT scans, with slimmer augmented reality glasses. Gao Yujia, director of the new National University XG AI Centre, said better networks and AI could place the hologram on a patient more accurately than is possible by hand now. Gao also said that no AI deployed on 5G so far can give hospital-wide recommendations, and that such systems have worked only at small scale, such as on a single ward. NUH is already testing nursing robots, which are meant to help nurses handle an expected rise in patient numbers rather than replace them.

Articles.Title: Home-based patient care among AI applications being tested at next-gen 5G, 6G research centre

stories.Headline: Stocks plunge as midterm results send AI trade into a tailspin
stories.Summary:
Stocks fell sharply on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, after Democratic wins in key gubernatorial races raised concerns about tighter rules for data center projects. The sell-off hit AI infrastructure companies hardest, with CoreWeave dropping around 10%, while chipmakers Micron and Nvidia fell 7% and 3.17%. Microsoft and Amazon, by contrast, each rose more than 6% as the market digested the results. Investors appeared to be sorting companies by their ability to keep building amid possible new restrictions.

In Texas, Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has proposed a statewide moratorium on new data center permits, though projects already under construction would reportedly be exempt. Nomura said Democratic gubernatorial wins could slow new development through tighter permitting and regulation. The impact looks uneven, since much of the capacity expected in 2027 is already being built and would be largely shielded. Projects planned for 2028 face greater exposure to permitting delays and regulatory uncertainty, according to the firm.

JPMorgan's James Sullivan, who co-heads global fundamental research, said the split reflects differences in borrowing costs. He told CNBC that borrowing spreads have widened sharply for neocloud companies, leaving their cost of additional capital well above that of hyperscalers with more diversified customers and revenue. He also argued that existing capacity has become more valuable because new supply is constrained. BMI warned that a sharp slowdown in data center construction could produce a larger-than-expected drop in overall investment.

The pressure builds on a financing problem that predates the election. Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren fell at least 30% in October as credit markets tightened and raised doubts about how AI infrastructure projects would be funded. CoreWeave's five-year credit default swap spread has climbed past 1,100 basis points, signaling higher costs for investors seeking protection against a possible default. The articles suggest the key question now is which companies can finance their projects well enough to withstand tougher rules.

Articles.Title: Stocks plunge as midterm results send AI trade into a tailspin

stories.Headline: Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: Singapore charts course for AI risk management in financial services
stories.Summary:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore issued its Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management for Financial Institutions on 7 October, setting out detailed supervisory expectations for how financial institutions should govern, develop, deploy and monitor AI. The article, published by the IAPP on 5 November 2026, describes the guidelines as a steady step by a regulator that has long worked in this area. The guidelines are not yet fully in force, since governance and oversight requirements begin on 7 October 2027 and more operational life cycle and capability requirements follow from 7 October 2028. The author warns firms not to treat that timeline as a reason to delay their preparations. The MAS defines AI broadly, covering machine learning systems, foundation models, large language models, generative AI applications and AI agents.

Rule-based systems and other deterministic automation that do not learn or adapt generally fall outside the guidelines. The approach is proportionate and risk-based, so a simplified set of governance policies can apply to low-impact use cases. Even those institutions must keep oversight, define permitted and prohibited uses, maintain an inventory of deployed AI, and conduct periodic reviews and training. Use cases that may have a material impact require a more comprehensive set of governance and risk-management measures, scaled to the institution's size, complexity and risk.

Under the guidelines, ultimate responsibility for AI risk management sits with senior management rather than a standalone compliance function. Senior managers must implement the framework, including escalation and incident management processes, and decide how resources are allocated. The article says organizations must keep clear records of AI deployment, identifying use cases, maintaining an AI inventory and conducting a risk materiality assessment. The guidelines also cover data management, transparency and fairness, human oversight, selection and testing, technology and cybersecurity, post-deployment monitoring, and retirement of systems.

The MAS is clear that outsourcing AI development, deployment or hosting does not reduce an institution's responsibility for the risks involved. The author notes that third-party contracts raise particular concerns for privacy professionals, especially whether vendors or their upstream model providers may retain, access or use customer data to train or improve models. Although the guidelines focus on financial services, the author argues that digital responsibility professionals in other sectors can learn from them as more AI rules emerge. The article frames the guidelines as a practical map of the risks that any organization deploying AI at scale will need to manage.

Articles.Title: Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: Singapore charts course for AI risk management in financial services

stories.Headline: Arista Lines Up Networking For 10 Gigawatts Of AI Systems
stories.Summary:
Arista Networks used its third-quarter earnings call, held in early November 2026, to lay out how far its networking business has moved into artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company's chief executive, Jayshree Ullal, told Wall Street analysts that Arista is working with AMD, Arm, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Qualcomm on rack-scale switching built on its Etherlink lines. She also said Arista expects trials of scale-up networks using the ESUN protocol to begin in 2027, with production rollouts following in 2028. Those scale-up networks would connect accelerators inside a rack and across a row, a segment where Arista has not yet earned significant revenue.

The reporting explains why this matters now. AI workloads are latency sensitive, and GPUs and other accelerators are expensive enough that leaving them idle is costly, so these clusters need flatter, higher-radix networks than earlier cloud designs. Arista's quarterly figures show the shift is already visible in revenue. In the September quarter the company posted product sales of $3.19 billion, up 66.9 percent from a year earlier, and services revenue of $467.6 million, up 17.9 percent. Total revenue reached $3.66 billion, up 58.5 percent, while net income rose 82.9 percent to $1.56 billion, which the article puts at 42.7 percent of revenue, the highest profit level in the company's history.

Looking ahead, Ullal said Arista expects to sell about $3.5 billion in AI front-end and back-end networking gear and services in 2026, and roughly $7 billion in 2027. Campus switching is forecast to reach $1.25 billion this year and $2 billion next year. On the midpoint of those targets, overall revenue would climb 52 percent to $13.3 billion in 2026, then 39.1 percent to $18.5 billion in 2027. The author notes that the non-AI parts of the business are growing more slowly, with the routing segment, which handles links between datacenters, driving much of the current growth. Ullal also said Arista has more than 100 customers using its AI-focused Etherlink switches and expects to provide networking for 10 gigawatts of AI cluster capacity by the end of 2027.

The article's author, who writes for The Next Platform, frames the outlook as cautious about timing. He argues that scale-up networking is still years from broad adoption and that Nvidia's proprietary NVLink and NVSwitch stack currently leads, though he expects open alternatives based on Ethernet and UALink to compete over time. Arista has not said it will adopt UALink switching, though third-party UALink chips from several vendors are available. What comes next, the article suggests, depends on how the 2027 scale-up trials perform and whether Arista adds one or two more large customers, which Ullal said might happen in the coming year.

Articles.Title: Arista Lines Up Networking For 10 Gigawatts Of AI Systems

stories.Headline: NCS programme doubles reach, bringing AI and coding skills to more lower-income pupils
stories.Summary:
NCS gave more than 130 primary pupils from lower-income families hands-on lessons in artificial intelligence, coding and robotics on Oct 31 at its NCS Hub in Ang Mo Kio. The event was the largest edition yet of N-Able Me!, the company's flagship corporate social responsibility initiative, and it marked a doubling of the programme's reach in its fourth year. The pupils, all in Primary 3 to 6, took part in practical sessions rather than traditional lectures. The programme aims to narrow the digital divide by giving children from lower-income families early exposure to technology.

The curriculum included a three-hour Micro:bit workshop in which pupils learned coding basics and worked in teams to build simple games. Each participant took home a Micro:bit device to support learning beyond the event. At a Superhero AI and Robotics Booth, children used an app developed by NCS employees to create AI-generated images of themselves as superheroes pursuing their dream jobs. A 1½-hour AI masterclass introduced foundational machine learning and prompt engineering, and robotics activities let pupils see hardware engineering up close.

NCS said the programme was run by a team of company tech volunteers and supported by strategic partners including the Ministry of Social and Family Development, ComLink+, Yayasan MENDAKI and The Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund. Senior Minister of State for Social and Family Development and Home Affairs Goh Pei Ming, the guest of honour, encouraged the participants and presented them with completion certificates. Goh said that when government, community and corporate partners work together, children can be given a better start. NCS chief executive Sam Liew said technology should be an inclusive enabler whose benefits reach everyone.

The pocket money fund, started in 2000 by The Straits Times, provides financial relief to children and youth from lower-income families and has helped more than 230,000 cases to date. Under the scheme, primary pupils receive $65 a month, secondary students receive $100 a month, and those in ITEs, junior colleges and polytechnics receive $125 a month. Liew said the aim is to equip young people with foundational tools so they can see themselves as builders in the AI era. The articles do not say whether the programme will expand further or when the next edition will take place.

Articles.Title: NCS programme doubles reach, bringing AI and coding skills to more lower-income pupils

stories.Headline: Everyone should assume they are under attack: Circle CEO on AI's risk to US infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire warned in a Yahoo Finance interview that everyone should assume they are under attack as frontier AI raises risks to critical infrastructure. Speaking on November 5, 2026, he said the risk environment is accelerating dramatically. He tied the shift to the point, roughly six months earlier, when agentic computing began to work at scale. The comments came as Circle reported its third-quarter results.

Allaire said the threat applies well beyond crypto, reaching hospitals, energy systems, utilities and financial firms. In his view, the risk calls for a completely different operating model and a new coordination between the private and public sectors. He described the threat vectors as among the most intense the world has seen. Circle's own numbers were strong, with total revenue and reserve income of $865 million, up 17% year over year, and adjusted operating profit up 85% to $317 million.

The company also reported that on-chain transaction volume for its USDC stablecoin rose 49% year over year to a record $13.9 trillion, while average circulation grew 8% to $73.3 billion. Circle announced a $400 million all-stock deal to acquire the cross-border payments platform Tazapay. Despite the results, Circle's stock fell 12% in midday trading on Thursday and is down 4% for the year. The article does not describe any specific attack or any government response to Allaire's warning.

Articles.Title: Everyone should assume they are under attack: Circle CEO on AI's risk to US infrastructure

stories.Headline: Stock Market Today: Rotation Away From AI Stocks Increases as Money Flows to AI Landlords
stories.Summary:
On Tuesday, Democrats took control of both the House and the Senate, and voters also rejected AI data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures, according to CNBC. By Wednesday's close, Amazon had jumped 8% and Apple had risen nearly 7%, while chipmakers fell sharply. Early Thursday trading showed the S&P 500 roughly flat, with funds tracking the index up 0.1% as of about 8:20 a.m. ET, though the index was splitting between its two halves.

Investors appear to have concluded that the AI buildout will now proceed more slowly and at higher cost, which helps companies that already own data center capacity and hurts the firms that sell them chips. NVIDIA was down 2% before the bell and had fallen 18% over the past month, while Intel was off 3% and had lost 51% in the same period. The leveraged Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF, known as SOXL, was indicated down 11%. Apple, trading near $354, also carries extra weight in the price-weighted Dow, which is why that index was leading the Nasdaq-100 higher or lower in the premarket.

Needham analyst Laura Martin said hyperscalers are AI incumbents, and Siebert Financial's Mark Malek said the most vulnerable AI companies are the borrowers rather than the largest spenders. Neither analyst's comments were offered as a forecast for any specific stock. The VIX, Wall Street's gauge of expected volatility, was near 21, up about 3 points from a week earlier. The 10-year Treasury yield was just under 5%, keeping borrowing costs high for small caps in the Russell 2000.

The Federal Reserve was scheduled to release its policy statement at 2 p.m. ET, with the top of its target range at 4% going into the announcement. The articles say any hint about future rate cuts would likely move small caps and high-valuation tech the most. Investors will also be watching whether chip stocks steady as they assess how far state-level limits on data centers may reach.

Articles.Title: Stock Market Today: Rotation Away From AI Stocks Increases as Money Flows to AI Landlords

stories.Headline: Delhi HC orders takedown of AI-generated videos targeting CM Rekha Gupta
stories.Summary:
On Friday, November 6, 2026, the Delhi High Court ordered the removal of several social media posts and videos published by the Aam Aadmi Party that allegedly depicted Chief Minister Rekha Gupta in a defamatory and demeaning way through AI-generated images and deepfake videos. The order came from Justice Manoj Jain in a defamation suit Gupta filed against the party. The posts were reported to have appeared on AAP's official and verified social media accounts. Gupta's plea asked the court to restrain the party from publishing or circulating such content.

According to the plea, the material portrayed her as a liquor vendor, hawker and delivery agent and as head of a fictitious scheme called "Har Har Rekha or Ghar Ghar Theka Yojana." One video allegedly showed her serving drinks to men at night, while another showed AI-generated figures of her and the Deputy Chief Minister pouring liquor and ice cubes. Gupta's plea said the videos looked so real that they created a misleading impression of her involvement in selling and serving liquor. The court noted that one video posted on X on November 4 had reportedly drawn about 75,000 views, 1,600 likes and 470 reposts when its screenshot was taken.

Justice Jain said that the offensive portrayal of the Chief Minister through AI-generated videos could not be treated as permissible political satire. He distinguished healthy criticism and humour from content that attacks personal dignity, and said the posts in question crossed that line by being defamatory and offensive to a woman holding constitutional office. He added that satire may hurt an individual but cannot be allowed to cause irreparable harm to dignity or reduce a person to an object of ridicule. The court also observed that holding public office invites greater scrutiny, yet does not permit the compromise of an individual's dignity.

Referring to earlier decisions, including the Raghav Chadha case, it said that until legislation regulates AI-generated content, courts must examine whether such use infringes the right to dignity. The court issued notices to all defendants, including AAP, and listed the matter for further hearing on December 4, 2026. The articles do not report any response from AAP to the order or to the allegations. They also do not say whether the content has already been removed from the platforms.

Articles.Title: Delhi HC orders takedown of AI-generated videos targeting CM Rekha Gupta

stories.Headline: This Little-Known Semiconductor Stock Has a Big AI Connection
stories.Summary:
Rambus, a little-known semiconductor company, has drawn attention from analysts at 24/7 Wall St. because it supplies memory interface chips that AI servers depend on. The article notes that the stock trades at $85.54, down about 20% over the past month, even though the company reported record third-quarter product revenue. Its price target is $128.10, which implies roughly 49.75% upside over the next twelve months. The stock is well below its 52-week high of $174.10 and near its low of $77.89.

Rambus leads the market for DDR5 registered clock drivers, the chips that sit on every server memory module. Third-quarter revenue reached $218.29 million, up 22.3% and above the $213.02 million consensus, and non-GAAP earnings per share of $0.84 beat the $0.79 estimate. Management guided fourth-quarter revenue to $227 million to $233 million and repurchased $135.4 million of stock during the quarter. The company also sees a $600 million opportunity in MRDIMM products as server platforms move from 8 memory channels to 12 or 16.

CEO Luc Seraphin said on the earnings call that the company sees demand strengthening as it looks into 2027. The article attributes the growth outlook to the company's own management and presents it as the basis for the optimistic view. It also raises concerns, noting that royalty guidance of $68 million to $74 million is below the third quarter's $76.96 million and that inventory rose to $74.8 million from $44.1 million. Management described the inventory build as deliberate, a response to customers ordering earlier to secure supply.

The article compares Rambus with Micron Technology, which trades at about 5 times forward earnings, and Marvell Technology, which trades at about 26 times. Rambus trades at about 24 times forward earnings and has a higher non-GAAP operating margin of 47%. Its bull case reaches $175.66 and its bear case falls to $110.70. The article warns that the forecasts depend on continued execution of the DDR5 and HBM roadmap and could be undermined by a downturn in the DRAM cycle or a cut in AI spending.

Articles.Title: This Little-Known Semiconductor Stock Has a Big AI Connection

stories.Headline: ‘Total repudiation’: The blue wave is about to hit AI
stories.Summary:
On Tuesday night, Democrats took control of the House and the Senate in the midterm elections, and a blue wave swept through traditionally red and swing states. Voters in several races, including the governor contests in Georgia and New Mexico, pressed a common theme of holding AI companies accountable. The article describes the result as a major setback for the AI industry, which now faces the prospect of new regulation and slower data center construction. Publicly, the major AI company CEOs have stayed mostly quiet, and OpenAI and Anthropic did not comment to The Verge.

Local data center moratorium measures appeared on ballots, and 43 of 44 passed, sending a clear signal to AI companies. Gina Hinojosa, the governor-elect of Texas, has said she plans to issue a moratorium on all data center approvals until the legislature can pass laws to protect Texans. Polling by NBC News found that 76 percent of voters opposed data centers in their communities. Residents have raised concerns about noise, electricity bill increases, and other effects, and the article says the opposition crosses party lines.

Wes McEnany, a former Senate committee staffer who now works with the Future of Life Institute, called the results a total repudiation of the AI field. Shaunna Thomas of the Guardrails Alliance called the data center backlash one of the most bipartisan issues she has seen. Kyle Jacobs-Morse of The Tech Oversight Project said voters linked rising power bills to big tech companies. Katie Barr, a consultant, cautioned against reading the results as an outright rejection of technology and said they reflect concerns about affordability, jobs, and safety.

Experts quoted in the article say the results likely end repeated Republican efforts to block state-level AI restrictions, and they expect more tech accountability bills. The article also reports that analysts expect major hurdles for AI legislation and a slowdown in planned data center construction, though they see a possible upside in avoiding an AI bubble. AI safety is expected to receive more attention, with Senator Jon Ossoff and Senator Mark Warner citing the issue, and President Trump has dismissed AI safety concerns as a hoax. The article notes that Democrats still have open questions about their next steps on tech policy.

Articles.Title: ‘Total repudiation’: The blue wave is about to hit AI

stories.Headline: Grimes to Make Feature Film Debut in Fully AI-Generated Movie, Lending Her Likeness and Real Voice (Exclusive)
stories.Summary:
Grimes is set to make her feature film debut in Gods Don't Give Gifts, a sci-fi anthology made entirely with artificial intelligence. The studio Fable and the YouTuber Gossip Goblin, whose real name is Zack London, announced the singer's involvement on Thursday, November 5, 2026. The film, which the producers describe as the first fully AI-generated feature to receive a theatrical release, is scheduled to open on December 4. Grimes lent her likeness and real voice to the project, which is made up of four interconnected short films.

Grimes, whose real name is Claire Boucher, will play Zayinth Alda, a disaffected aristocrat who visits a dealer of dreamspools in the slums of East Cinder. The film is set on the fictional world of Niiro Cradle, where bodies are disposable and consciousness has been commoditized. The team drew on Grimes's past fashion choices, including looks from the Met Gala, Coachella and her music videos, to shape the character's design. The character has long platinum-blonde hair, a skeletal mask with gold teeth and a metallic, ribcage-like breastplate. It is still unclear how large a role she will have, since she appeared only briefly in the trailer released October 6.

London and the producer Edward Saatchi made the announcement and shared details of Grimes's involvement in statements to People. London said he has been a fan of her music since college and described the team's process of floating character designs with her before settling on the final look. Saatchi said her participation is the first time a performer of her stature has appeared in an AI movie. He also said the project aims to set a new visual style for animated films and to show performers driving characters that look nothing like those in traditional studio animation.

The project is also aiming for recognition beyond its theatrical release. According to Variety, Fable plans to submit the film for Best Animated Feature consideration at the Academy Awards. The Academy's rules say AI use neither helps nor harms a film's chances, but that voters will weigh how much a human was at the heart of the creative work. The rules also allow the Academy to ask for more information about how generative AI was used. The film's synopsis describes four stories framed by an ancient AI and linked by a street preacher who rails against technology overwriting humanity.

Articles.Title: Grimes to Make Feature Film Debut in Fully AI-Generated Movie, Lending Her Likeness and Real Voice (Exclusive)

stories.Headline: An AI Fraud Kingpin’s Confessions
stories.Summary:
Yuriy Nazarenko, the creator of the underground site OnlyFake, has spoken publicly for the first time about his role in a global fake identity operation. Writing for 404 Media on November 5, 2026, reporter Joseph Cox said Nazarenko described how he once forged documents by hand from a desk in his grandfather's apartment in Ukraine. Nazarenko then built a website that automated the process, and it later added generative AI to produce realistic photos of fake IDs. The site spread quickly through the fraud world, and the Department of Justice said it made more than a million dollars selling fake IDs for $15 each.

The article explains why these forgeries matter to criminals. A convincing scan of an identity document can help someone open bank accounts, get around identity checks on cryptocurrency exchanges, or rent a property while hiding their real identity. Cox reported that OnlyFake threatened the idea of know-your-customer checks, the steps financial institutions take to confirm who their clients are. Before OnlyFake, forging such documents took skill and many hours of work, but the site let anyone produce hundreds or thousands at a time for a few dollars in Bitcoin. Cox also noted that the site inspired copycats.

Nazarenko, now 28, pleaded guilty in the United States and served a year in prison. He is now living in Asia after months in ICE detention that followed his sentence. According to the article, he said North Korean fake IT workers used his creation, and he described panicking and destroying his laptop and emails after Cox's first report in 2024. The article is based on interviews with Nazarenko and his lawyer, court records, and Cox's own reporting on the online fraud world. Cox writes that the FBI arrested Nazarenko and shut down some competitors, and the article offers Nazarenko's own account of how the operation grew.

Articles.Title: An AI Fraud Kingpin’s Confessions

stories.Headline: Expedient adds multitenant cloud to its Nutanix partnership, with a governed AI on-ramp
stories.Summary:
Expedient, a Pittsburgh-based cloud service provider, announced on November 5, 2026 an expanded partnership with Nutanix that adds a multitenant deployment model to Expedient Cloud Powered by Nutanix. The move is aimed at lowering the barrier to a modern, fully managed cloud and giving organizations a route into governed artificial intelligence on the same platform. Nutanix's Inder Sidhu, the company's chief customer experience and partner officer, said the multitenant approach is meant to bring far more organizations into the Nutanix ecosystem. He described Expedient as a key service provider design partner in developing Nutanix SP Central.

Under the new model, each client receives a securely isolated environment on Nutanix infrastructure in Expedient data centers, and Expedient runs the platform with 24/7/365 support from U.S.-based staff. Because every deployment runs on AHV, the Nutanix hypervisor, workloads can move among on-premises, dedicated and multitenant environments without conversion. The announcement also says the Nutanix platform can run AI and containerized applications alongside traditional virtual machines, so organizations can move AI projects from pilot to production. Expedient's AI CTRL Platform delivers AI as a governed, cost-predictable managed service with integrated security and data-sovereignty controls. Clients can also add Expedient DRaaS, backup and colocation services across 14 U.S. data centers.

Expedient CEO Bryan Smith said organizations are placing each workload where it runs best for cost, performance and governance, and that now includes AI. He said Nutanix builds the platform while Expedient operationalizes it, leaving one partner accountable across multitenant, dedicated and edge cloud. Smith described the multitenant offering as the latest result of the two companies' joint work. Expedient also says it has earned the Powered by Nutanix: Verified Solutions qualification for its Dedicated Private Cloud, Multitenant Private Cloud and Disaster Recovery as a Service offerings.

Expedient describes itself as the first Nutanix Premier Service Provider and a two-time Nutanix Service Provider Partner of the Year for the Americas, and it notes it is one of 14 Broadcom Pinnacle tier VMware Cloud Service Providers in the U.S. The company backs its solutions with a 100% SLA and 24/7 access to U.S.-based engineers. Expedient also said it would host a webinar on November 5 at 1 p.m. ET to explain what the Nutanix multitenant offering means for customers. The announcement does not give pricing or customer adoption figures for the new service.

Articles.Title: Expedient Expands Partnership with Nutanix with Multitenant Cloud, Lowering the Barrier to Modern Cloud and Governed AI
